Managing a rising word-game grid

Manage Word Tile Rush’s 90-second countdown, adjacent letter paths, per-letter scoring, column settling, and row added after each accepted word.

By NoCharge·Reviewed by NoCharge·Published August 15, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Spell words. Clear the grid.

Play Word Tile RushBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: Word Tile Rush gives you 90 seconds after the first tile selection. Each accepted word scores one point per letter, clears its path, settles columns, and adds a row at the bottom.

The clock starts with a selection

The game begins with a six-by-eight grid and a 90-second display. Selecting the first tile starts the countdown. The clock continues while you build a path; selecting letters does not pause it. Use the game’s Pause control or leave the page hidden to suspend the active session when you need a break.

Trace a legal path, then submit

Each next letter must be in a neighboring cell, including a diagonal neighbor. A tile cannot be used twice in one path; returning to an earlier tile shortens the selection to that point. Submit an accepted word from the built-in list to score one point per letter.

How the grid rises

After an accepted word, its selected letters are removed. Remaining letters fall within their own columns, then a new row is inserted at the bottom. The grid does not rise on a repeating interval while you search; it changes after a valid submission. If letters occupy the top row after that change, the run ends. The timer reaching zero also ends the run.

Choose words with the current scoring rule

A longer accepted word earns more points because each letter is worth one point. There is no length-squared multiplier. A shorter word can still be useful if it is a clear accepted path, but the current score alone does not save or compare a personal best.

The current path, score, and remaining time are visible. Tile buttons, Submit word, and Clear path are standard controls; the game does not require drag input. For point examples, read How Word Tile Rush scoring works.
